Legacy suppression retains a placeholder justification

Gap: The changed #suppress message is still a FIXME placeholder, so it does not provide the justification required by the directive contract.

Expected

Suppress directive allows suppressing a specific warning diagnostic. It takes 2 arguments: The diagnostic code to suppress and a message to justify the suppression.

Behavior-affecting operationId suppression bypasses TypeSpec semantics

Gap: The changed code suppresses no-openapi to force wire operation IDs, but the fetched Azure guidance explicitly says behavior-affecting @operationId usage must not be suppressed.

Expected

Decorators that do affect behavior should never be suppressed: name your interface and operation accordingly instead of using @operationId, and define the types correctly in TypeSpec instead of using @useRef.

Guidance: Azure Core `no-openapi` rule
